title: Lacordaire (1850)
hookLine: a well-known preacher restores the Dominicans in France

cards: Paris. A cathedral full to the doors, and in the pulpit a young priest whose sermons don't sound like the ones people grew up with.
He talks about freedom, about doubt, about the questions students argue over late at night. People who hadn't set foot in a church in a long time come to Notre-Dame to hear him.

Then, at the height of it, he leaves for Rome. When he comes back, he is dressed in white: the habit of the Dominicans, an order the upheavals of the Revolution had pushed out of France. His name was Henri Lacordaire.

teach.h: HE BROUGHT THE FRIARS BACK TO FRANCE.
teach.b: Lacordaire took the religious name Dominique, after the founder, and set out to do something that sounded impossible: gather men to live as Dominican friars in France again. The way he did it is the lesson.
Yesterday's courts tried to force belief. Lacordaire went the other way.
Before he was a friar, he had helped run a newspaper arguing that the Church should ask nothing from governments except freedom: to teach, to gather, to preach.

teach.h: HE ACCEPTED THE RULING AND STAYED.
teach.b: When the pope rejected some of the paper's ideas, Lacordaire accepted the ruling and stayed. He didn't win by shouting, and he didn't leave by slamming the door.
When he asked for the friars to return, he appealed to the same liberty every citizen claimed, not to a special favor.
And when he preached, the story goes, he spoke to doubters as people worth talking to, not as enemies to defeat. The first letter of Peter puts it in two steps.
In the Douay-Rheims, believers are told to be "ready always to satisfy every one that asketh you a reason of that hope which is in you."
Then the next verse begins: "But with modesty and fear." A reason, and modesty.

teach.h: READY ALWAYS TO SATISFY EVERY ONE THAT ASKETH.
teach.b: Lacordaire held both. For him, preaching wasn't volume. It was respect with a reason inside it.

how: French Dominicans remember Lacordaire as the friar who restored their order in France, and some Catholic preachers still point to his Notre-Dame sermons as an example of speaking to people who doubt.

games.q: you're Lacordaire. you want the friars back in France, where they were shut down. how do you ask?
o: ask the government for a special privilege for the Church.
appeal to the same liberty every citizen claims.
wait quietly and hope someone else does it.
games.why: he asked for the freedom everyone claimed, not a special favor, and then came home in the habit.

practice: Bring to mind one person you disagree with about something that matters, faith or anything else.
Don't rehearse the argument; find one true, kind thing you could say to them first, and hold that sentence gently, like something breakable. If you pray, ask for modesty in the next conversation.

wordCard.voice: Lacordaire. The French preacher who became a Dominican friar and brought the order back to France, asking for freedom and speaking to doubters with respect. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: freedom. what Lacordaire asked for the Church and the friars: freedom, not favors.
